clue.text: Bird putting away pie has first-class beak

indicators.note: putting away means the bird's name loses the word pie that follows

parts.note: the magpie is a black and white bird
taken as written, the last three letters of the bird
first-rate, written 1st-rate with the figure 1 as the letter I

explanation.surface: A bird gobbles a pie and turns out to have a first-class bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beak' looks like the bird's bill but is British slang for a judge in a lower court. 'First-class' is 1ST-RATE with the 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Beak is old British slang for a justice of the peace sitting in a lower court.

clue.text: Minute clothing label is fake

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a minute
CK is the Calvin Klein fashion label

explanation.surface: A tiny label sewn into a garment gives away that it is counterfeit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like an adjective meaning tiny; it is the noun, a short time, giving MO.
explanation.definitionFit: A mock item is an imitation or sham, so fake in the adjectival sense.

clue.text: Peer's wife getting into crack

indicators.note: getting into means the wife's letter goes inside the word for crack

parts.note: a crack is a gap

explanation.surface: A nobleman's wife slips into a crack in the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a lord with a wife; it is the verb, to stare.
explanation.definitionFit: To peer is to look hard, and to gawp is to stare stupidly, so the verbs are close synonyms.

clue.text: One may forget how to get in bar?

parts.note: the instruction scatter the word brain produces the letters of 'in bar', so 'in bar' is what that instruction yields

explanation.surface: A forgetful person wonders how to get into the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, SCATTER BRAIN, and rearranging BRAIN gives IN BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A scatterbrain is a disorganised, absent-minded person, someone likely to forget things.

clue.text: What a recidivist does to get hashish, for example

definitions.meaning: cannabis ... is the sticky extract sold as hash

explanation.surface: A repeat offender lapses again just to get hold of some drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A recidivist falls back into crime, sinning once more; hashish is the resin of the cannabis plant.

clue.text: Art's lifted mood now, Keats reveals

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifted means the letters read upwards, from bottom to top
reveals means the letters are found inside the words mood now, Keats

explanation.surface: Keats's poetry raised the gloomy mood: art lifts the spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reveals' finds ODNOWKEAT spanning 'mood now, Keats'; 'lifted' turns it upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Taekwondo is a Korean martial art, so it is an example of an art.

clue.text: President's eighth vehicle?

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
H is the eighth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: The question asks which car is the president's eighth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eighth' is not a count of vehicles but the eighth letter, H.
explanation.definitionFit: Two US presidents, George H W Bush and his son George W Bush, bore this surname.

clue.text: More possibly out playing with key player

indicators.note: playing means the letters of out are moved about, playing around

parts.note: a pianist plays the keys

explanation.surface: A musician tries a piece with a pianist, perhaps going off more freely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' is Sir Thomas More, author of Utopia; 'out' rearranged gives UTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More wrote Utopia, describing an ideal society, so he could be called an idealist of that kind.

clue.text: Make uniform in nursing terribly soigné

indicators.note: nursing means holding something inside, as a nurse cradles a baby

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: terribly means the letters of soigné are badly jumbled

parts.note: soigné means well groomed

explanation.surface: A uniform worn in a care home is terribly smart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' here means at home, and 'nursing' has that word hold the jumbled letters, OGENIS, made by 'terribly'.
explanation.definitionFit: To homogenise is to make something the same throughout, evenly blended.

clue.text: Cop working with lawyers is a plant

indicators.note: working means the letters of cop and lawyers are set to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A police officer teamed up with lawyers turns out to be an informer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a spy planted among them, but it is the hedgerow flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Cow parsley is a common white-flowered wild herb of verges and hedgerows.

clue.text: Somewhere to kip either side of Dagenham

indicators.note: either side of means the two end letters of Dagenham stand on each flank of the middle piece

parts.note: only its two end letters, D and M, are used, one on each side
either pairs with or, so this word gives the letters OR

explanation.surface: Looking for a place to sleep on either side of Dagenham, in east London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'either side of Dagenham' reads cryptically as 'D or M': the outer letters of Dagenham with OR between. Dagenham is a district of east London.
explanation.definitionFit: A dorm, short for dormitory, is a room of beds, a place to sleep.

clue.text: Six leaner and sporting six-footers

indicators.note: sporting means the letters of six leaner and are shown off in a lively new arrangement

explanation.surface: Six lean athletes, all tall and sporty, stand around six feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footers' looks like tall people; it means verse lines of six metrical feet.
explanation.definitionFit: An alexandrine is a line of verse with six iambic feet, twelve syllables in all.

clue.text: Delaying, blocking one with this tactic?

indicators.note: blocking means the delaying word stands round the other pieces, closing them in

parts.note: stalling means delaying

explanation.surface: Someone stalls proceedings, obstructing an opponent with a stalling tactic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delaying' looks like the definition but builds the outer part; the whole clue then describes the tactic, so the definition leans on the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonewalling is obstructive stalling, refusing to answer or cooperate, and in cricket purely defensive batting.

clue.text: Fighter protects old man where work is rough

indicators.note: protects means the fighter wraps around the father, shielding him

parts.note: a scrapper is someone who fights
old man is slang for father, pa

explanation.surface: A boxer guards his father in a rough workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough work' is draft jottings, not hard labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrap paper is used for rough notes and drafts, so rough work goes on it.

clue.text: Deep Throat may reveal this stuff in dodgy toilets

indicators.note: in places the eating word inside the jumbled toilets
dodgy means the letters of toilets are unreliable and rearranged

parts.note: to stuff oneself is to pig

explanation.surface: The notorious film is stashed in some seedy public lavatories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges TOILETS into ELOTTIS, with PIG put 'in'. Deep Throat was a 1972 pornographic film.
explanation.definitionFit: The epiglottis is the flap at the back of the throat, visible deep in a wide-open mouth.

clue.text: Mafia boss hides cockney behind new decorative covering

indicators.note: hides means the mafia boss conceals the backside within himself

parts.note: a capo is a Mafia chief
aris is cockney rhyming slang for bottom (Aristotle, bottle, bottle and glass, arse)

explanation.surface: A Mafia boss covers his backside with a fancy new cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang: Aristotle rhymes with bottle, and bottle and glass rhymes with arse, shortened to ARIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A caparison is an ornamental cloth draped over a horse, a decorative cover.

clue.text: Ripping story about shipwreck in shaky grounds

indicators.note: about means the torn-up story goes round the wrecked ship
ripping means the letters of story are torn apart and rearranged
wreck means the letters of ship are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A thrilling yarn about a shipwreck turns out to have flimsy foundations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shipwreck' splits into the fodder and its signal 'wreck', making PHIS; 'Ripping' scrambles 'story' into SOTRY, which goes 'about' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophistry is clever but fallacious reasoning, argument resting on unsound grounds.

clue.text: Reverse of zero times this is number 54

indicators.note: reverse of means the words for zero and times are written backwards together

parts.note: none means zero
the multiplication sign X means times

explanation.surface: A sum: reverse zero, multiply, and you reach fifty-four.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse of' turns NONE X round; 'number 54' is an atomic number, not the result of the sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenon is the chemical element with atomic number 54.

clue.text: Put out Scottish team to get stripped off

indicators.note: stripped off means the team name loses its outer letters

parts.note: Rangers is a Glasgow football club

explanation.surface: A Scottish football team undresses after being sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped off' takes the first and last letters off RANGERS, a Glasgow football club.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone out is to annoy or offend them, which is to make them cross.

clue.text: Rock music's inspiring No 1s in prospect

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so these letters take in the numbers

parts.note: prog is progressive rock
's stands for is
No is short for number, so Nos are numbers

explanation.surface: A rock band's music inspires a string of chart-toppers in future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No 1s' looks like hit records; it is the plural abbreviation NOS for numbers, breathed in by PROG IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A prognosis is a forecast of the likely outcome, a prospect of what lies ahead.

clue.text: Favouring mine, one a politician's appeasing

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a pit is a mine
I is the Roman numeral one
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A politician supports reopening a mine to placate voters.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Propitiatory describes something meant to win favour or placate, so it is conciliatory.

clue.text: Knocked back pill, red and sweet

indicators.note: knocked back means swallowed, and in a down entry the letters read from the bottom up

parts.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet
a Trot, short for Trotskyist, is a left-wing red

explanation.surface: Someone swallowed a pill and some red wine, then had pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' looks like drinking; it reverses E TROT.
explanation.definitionFit: A torte is a rich layered cake, served as a dessert, which British English calls a sweet.

clue.text: One seabird's rising, another's coming down

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: an auk is a seabird, and auk's, with the apostrophe dropped, gives AUKS

explanation.surface: Two seabirds: one climbs into the sky while the other dives down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming down' refers to the entry being a down light; the answer is the other bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The skua is a predatory seabird, so it is another seabird besides the auk.

clue.text: Python seized by intrepid lemur

indicators.note: seized by means the letters are held inside the words intrepid lemur

explanation.surface: A snake grabbed by a fearless lemur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Python' is not the snake but one of the Monty Python team.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Idle was a member of the Monty Python comedy troupe.

clue.text: Stroke sheep's back and goat's back

indicators.note: back means the word for the sheep is read backwards

parts.note: a tup is a ram

indicators.note: the goat's back means the last letter of goat

explanation.surface: Petting animals: stroke a sheep's back and a goat's back.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'back's do different jobs: the first reverses TUP, the second takes the last letter of 'goat's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A putt is a gentle stroke in golf, played on the green.

clue.text: Jack and Kelvin slicing wound that's not dressed

indicators.note: slicing means the sailor and kelvin cut into the twisted word

parts.note: wound, from wind, means twisted, snaked
jack tar is a sailor, so jack gives TAR
K is the symbol for kelvin

explanation.surface: A sailor and a man named Kelvin cut into a wound left undressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' looks like an injury and 'dressed' like a bandage; it is the past tense of wind, SNAKED.
explanation.definitionFit: Stark naked means completely nude, with no clothes on at all.

clue.text: Got up in something between red and white

definitions.meaning: past tense of to stand up or ascend
a pink colour, a mix of red and white

explanation.surface: Someone got up wearing something pinkish.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise is to get up, past tense; rose is also a pinkish colour midway between red and white.

clue.text: Promote latest odds in contest, which has many dimensions

parts.note: to hype is to promote heavily

indicators.note: in places the betting abbreviation inside the contest

parts.note: a race is a contest
SP, the starting price, is the final odds when a race begins

explanation.surface: A bookmaker promotes the latest odds on a race of many stages.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, starting price, is the betting term for the final odds when a race starts.
explanation.definitionFit: In science fiction and maths, hyperspace is a realm of more than three dimensions.
